solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sensitive European male, obstructing boxing knuckle-head

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the obstructing word holds the fool inside it

parts.note: barring a way is obstructing it
a knucklehead is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A touchy European man is in a ring, getting in the way of a dim-witted boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knuckle-head' looks like part of the boxing scene but is just the fool, and 'boxing' is the containment signal, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive matter is an awkward, cringe-making one, which is what an embarrassing topic is.

clue.text: Scrap former husband? Safe bet accepting relationship's end

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the safe bet holds the final letter

parts.note: a cert, short for certainty, is a racing term for a safe bet

indicators.note: the end of the word relationship is its last letter

explanation.surface: Is a former husband just scrap, a safe bet once the relationship ends?
explanation.walkthrough: CERT is racing slang for a certainty, a horse sure to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap of text is a short extract or passage taken from a longer work.

clue.text: Material for piece over aeroplane nose?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a slab is a thick piece or chunk

indicators.note: the nose of the aeroplane is its front, so its first letter

explanation.surface: A query about what to make the nose cone of a model aeroplane from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns SLAB to BALS; 'nose' gives the A that starts 'aeroplane'.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood, the classic material for model aircraft.

clue.text: Tough inmate left one for dead

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one thing replaces another

parts.note: a resident is one who lives in a place, as an inmate does
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hard prisoner abandoned a fellow inmate, leaving him for dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' swaps D in RESIDENT for LI, giving RESILIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tough bounces back from hardship; resilient describes exactly that hardiness.

clue.text: Entrances missing tenor's solo

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the tenor letter is taken away

parts.note: atria are entrance halls, the plural of atrium

explanation.surface: A singer misses his cue on stage, so the tenor's solo goes unheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' reads as a stage term or a verb for enchanting; it is ATRIA, entrance halls.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, often given to the tenor.

clue.text: Troops join army finally holding unit

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the unit sits inside the rest

parts.note: to solder is to join metal pieces
I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of army

explanation.surface: Troops enlist in the army, ending up attached to a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is a collective noun for soldiers, a body of troops.

clue.text: Suggestion's grand, undressed?

indicators.note: 's stands for 'is': the grand is undressed, i.e. it is in the word for naked

parts.note: undressed means naked, wearing nothing at all, in the altogether
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A suggestive remark: the piano is grand, and so is someone wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read ''s grand, undressed' as 'grand is in the nude': being in the nude puts G inside NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod or hint to act is a suggestion, which is what a nudge is.

clue.text: Endless impregnation ends well without sex

indicators.note: the ends of impregnation are its first and last letters
without means outside, so the healthy word goes around the sex word

parts.note: fine means well, in good health
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a pregnancy achieved without sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, an old sense, not lacking; 'it' is a coy euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infinite has no limit, so it never comes to an end.

clue.text: Caught inside covers, usually playing

indicators.note: the letters are caught inside the words covers, usually, held within them

explanation.surface: Cricket: a batsman caught in the covers, as usually happens while playing.
explanation.walkthrough: COVERS is a cricket fielding position, which makes the surface look like a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Team A playing team B is the same match as team A versus team B: against.

clue.text: Church, in case nearly full, accepting one's divine

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
lest means in case, for fear that

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word is cut short by a letter

parts.note: all means the full amount
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A church that's nearly full, in case one feels divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepting' takes the numeral into the whole string, so it lands between the 'in case' word and the shortened 'full'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means heavenly, belonging to the gods, so divine is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Play Hamlet, perhaps taking Claudius's lead

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding the letter inside

parts.note: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, an example of a Dane

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor playing Hamlet takes his cue from Claudius on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like the drama; it is a verb, as light plays on water.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance is to move lightly and playfully, as light plays or dances on water.

clue.text: Very, very undressed flipping partner

indicators.note: flipping means the remaining letters are turned round
undressed means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle

parts.note: an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone very, very undressed, flipping their partner around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undressed' strips VERY to ER; 'flipping' makes it RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Really used as an intensifier means very, as in really good.

clue.text: Composer's relative replacing another composer's intro

indicators.note: replacing, with intro, means one piece takes the place of the opening letter

parts.note: Frederick Delius was an English composer
a sib is a sibling, a relative

explanation.surface: A composer's relative takes over the introduction of another composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing' puts SIB in place of the D that opens DELIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was the Finnish composer of Finlandia and seven symphonies.

clue.text: Try endlessly to have comfort in puzzle

indicators.note: to have means to hold, so the comfort word goes inside
endlessly means the last letter of try is dropped

parts.note: to ease is to comfort

explanation.surface: Try not to stop until you find comfort in a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like a verb or synonym to find; the two letters left of the word itself are what hold the comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser, short for brainteaser, is a tricky puzzle.

clue.text: Incomprehensible swearing includes satire, oddly

indicators.note: includes means the swearing holds the picked letters

parts.note: abuse is insulting, swearing language

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of satire

explanation.surface: Swearing that includes satire, strangely, is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means obscure, difficult to understand, close to incomprehensible.

clue.text: Left back races after spoils

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
hies is an old verb meaning hurries, races

explanation.surface: A left-back footballer chases trophies after the matches.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the nautical word for left; HIE is an archaic verb for hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophies are prizes taken in victory, and spoils are the booty a winner carries off.

clue.text: Francis Drake, say, seizing endless gear on vessel?

definitions.text: Francis Drake, say, seizing endless gear on vessel?

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the noble takes the rest inside

parts.note: Drake, a famous Elizabethan grandee, is offered as an example of a noble, a peer

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of rig goes

parts.note: rig means gear or outfit
a vat is a large vessel or tank

explanation.surface: Drake grabs equipment from a ship, as a licensed raider would.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer; the blog notes Drake was knighted, not ennobled, so calling him a noble is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake sailed under royal licence to seize enemy ships and cargo, the role of a licensed raider.

clue.text: Income from work turning in unevenly selected rates

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the selected letters
unevenly selected takes the odd-numbered letters of rates
turning means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a piece is a work, as of art or music

explanation.surface: Income from work, with rates calculated unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' gives ECEIP, which goes inside R, T, S, taken from 'rates' by 'unevenly selected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are money taken in by a business, its takings or income.

clue.text: Intoxicated and hammered around start of opening time

indicators.note: around means the beaten word goes round the other letters

parts.note: bested means beaten, hammered

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of opening

explanation.surface: Drunk and hammered by the time the pub opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' looks like a second word for drunk; it means beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Besotted means infatuated, and in an older sense stupefied with drink, intoxicated.

clue.text: Bother, does my bum look big in this?

definitions.meaning: fuss and commotion, as in hustle and fuss

definitions.text: does my bum look big in this?
definitions.meaning: a padded frame worn under a Victorian skirt to bulk out the behind, so the answer to the question is surely yes

explanation.surface: An exasperated sigh, then the classic anxious question about how an outfit looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustle is both fuss and busy activity, and the padded pad that enlarged the rear of a Victorian dress.

clue.text: Cuts queues outside front of train

indicators.note: outside means the queues go round the other letter

parts.note: files are lines of people, queues

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of train

explanation.surface: Someone cuts the queues at the front of the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Filets, or fillets, are boneless cuts of meat or fish.

clue.text: Chief certain the compiler's about top at last

indicators.note: about means around, so the certain word goes round a letter

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of top

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to himself as me; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: The setter is certain he is about to come out on top at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank, the chief or paramount one.

clue.text: Fragments blow grenade core in unfinished projectile

indicators.note: in places the blow and core inside the cut-down projectile
unfinished means the last letter of shell is dropped

parts.note: a shell is an explosive projectile
a rap is a sharp blow

indicators.note: core means the central letter of grenade

explanation.surface: Fragments from a blast as a grenade's core goes off inside a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is the metal fragments thrown out by an exploding shell or bomb.

clue.text: Paved area typically installed outside initially

definitions.text: Paved area typically installed outside initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of each of the clue's words are taken

explanation.surface: A paved area is typically put in outside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paved area' is also the definition, so the whole clue both defines and spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor space beside a house, typically laid outside.

clue.text: Computer to put in last of Excel program

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of Excel
put in means placed inside, so the word to goes inside the program

parts.note: an app is a program, short for application

explanation.surface: Install the last of the Excel program on your computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Excel is a spreadsheet program, which makes the computing surface feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer.

clue.text: For consumption get pulse taken in digit

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the pulse word goes inside

parts.note: consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, abbreviated TB
to hum is to throb or pulse with energy

explanation.surface: To check for consumption, get your pulse taken at the finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as the pulse being taken by a doctor, but signals containment; consumption is the old name for tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb is one of the five digits of the hand.

clue.text: Line from fabulous bird stood up on date

indicators.note: on means placed after in a down clue
stood up means the word is set upright, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend

explanation.surface: A line from a mythical bird who was stood up on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is a length of string or rope, a line.

clue.text: Virtuoso pianist's record capturing Bizet's essence

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of, so the record goes round the letter

parts.note: a list is a written record

indicators.note: essence means the central letter of Bizet

explanation.surface: A virtuoso pianist's recording captures the very heart of Bizet's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the great 19th-century Hungarian concert virtuoso of the keyboard.

clue.text: Get to hold bleeding heart in routine

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the getting word goes around

parts.note: to procure is to get or obtain

indicators.note: heart means the central letters of bleeding

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a bleeding heart in a routine operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' gives ED, the middle two of 'bleeding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established way of doing something, a routine.

clue.text: Great guy hosting party with touching Queen cover

indicators.note: hosting means holding guests inside, so the rope holds the rest

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable steadying a tent or mast

indicators.note: cover means surround, so the touching word and the Queen letter go round the party

parts.note: on means touching, concerning
R is the abbreviation for Queen, from Regina
a side is a party or faction

explanation.surface: A great man hosts a party where he touches up the Queen's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With ... cover' means the touching word and the Queen letter go either side of the party, and that sits inside the rope after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means large or substantial, so great in size or amount.
